the Ca2+-regulated thin filaments of smooth muscle are made up of four proteins: actin, tropomysin, caldesmon, and a Ca2+ binding regulatory protein (CaBP).
a novel Ca2+-binding smooth muscle protein (CaBP), identical to calmodulin, is associated with the Ca2+-regulated thin filaments of smooth muscle.
CaBP is a novel Ca2+-binding smooth muscle protein that is structurally altered calmodulin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism by which Ca2+ activates thin filaments in smooth muscle.
the regulation of smooth muscle thin filams by Ca2+ and caldesmon, and the identification of a Ca2+-regulated protein in smooth muscle thin filas.
the regulation of the contractile machinery in smooth muscle and the mechanism by which the Ca2+-regulated thin filament is assembled.

CaBP is CaM in a metastable conformation.

CaBP is not CaM, but a structurally altered CaM.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CaBP is CaM in an altered state that is stabilized by interaction with caldesmon and tropomyosim.
calmodulin can exist in at least three distinct states: the normal, the CaBP and a heat labile intermediate state.

CaBP has a special structure which makes it different from other forms of calmodulin.
